# GAPS

<!-- generated by `iut gaps --md` from src/iut_gaps.c — do not edit -->

What the papers specify and the toolkit does not do the way the papers do it: 25 entries, of which 13 are open, 3 approximate, 3 asserted and 6 fixed.
`iut gaps` prints this table, `iut pipeline` prints the entries of each stage under that stage, and `IUT_GAP("Id")` marks the places in the sources.
The review behind it is in [gaps/GAP_REPORT.md](gaps/GAP_REPORT.md) and [gaps/REVIEW_LOG.md](gaps/REVIEW_LOG.md).

* **open**: not computed at all; a placeholder stands in.
* **approximate**: computed from bounds or estimates, and labelled as such.
* **asserted**: taken as an input (a flag, a constant, a theorem), not checked.
* **fixed**: was a gap or a mistake; closed, kept for the record.

| id | status | what the papers specify | what the code does | where | the fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HodgeTheatersAreBookkeeping`<br>Hodge theaters are records of labels and copy numbers | open | Categories: tempered Frobenioids F̲_v, their base categories D_v = B^temp(Π_v)^0, global Frobenioids F^⊛_mod, poly-isomorphisms as sets of isomorphisms, bridges as poly-morphisms of capsules. <br>*[IUTchI] §3–§6; [EtTh]; [FrdI], [FrdII]; [AbsTopIII]* | A prime-strip is, per v, a tuple of copy numbers (Π_v, G_v, O×) and a list of valuations; a bridge is a flag; a poly-isomorphism is a flag `full_poly_isomorphism` and, in iut_i.c, a count. | iut_core.c: iut_prime_strip_build, iut_hodge_theater_new; iut_i.c | Open, and by design of the data model (docs/DATA_MODEL.md §8). A first real step: represent Π_v at v ∈ V^bad by generators of the tempered fundamental group of the Tate curve and G_v by its (p, e, f) invariants, so that an isomorphism of prime-strips is an actual map. |
| `GlobalNumberFieldElements`<br>No element of F_mod^× or κ-coric function is ever written down | open | The monoid M^⊛_mod = F_mod^×, the κ-coric rational functions on C_K and their values at the strictly critical points, which give the NF-bridge its content. <br>*[IUTchI] Ex 5.1, Def 5.2; Rem 3.1.7* | Pseudo-monoids are described by name and by Kummer-ready/Kummer-blind flags; the κ-coric check takes a caller-supplied description of a function. | iut_i.c: iut_pseudo_monoid_get, iut_kappa_coric_check | Open. For F_mod = Q a rational-function type with exact coefficients would do; the global Kummer theory of Prop 3.10 then becomes a statement about real elements. |

## Stage 3, Gaussian monoids

| id | status | what the papers specify | what the code does | where | the fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ThetaValuesOrdersOnly`<br>Theta values are orders and units of q^{j²}, not values of the theta function | approximate | The étale theta function Θ̲_v evaluated at the l-torsion points labelled j gives q̲_v^{j²} = (q_v^{1/2l})^{j²} up to μ_2l, an element of K_v. <br>*[IUTchII] Cor 2.5, 2.6, 3.5; [EtTh] Prop 1.4* | The order j²·ord(q_v)/2l is exact, and the unit of q_v^{j²} is computed mod p^8 from the Tate parameter. The 2l-th root q̲_v and the theta series itself are not computed. | iut_pipeline.c: stage 3; iut_input.c: iut_tate_unit_pow; iut_ops_iv.c: iut_gap_theta_value | Prepared: iut_gap_theta_value is the placeholder. Extracting the 2l-th root needs K_v (gap LocalFieldsOfK); once K_v = F_v(ζ_l, q^{1/l}) is represented, q̲ is a uniformizer power times a unit by Hensel, and the series Σ (−1)^n q^{(n²+n)/2}(U^{2n+1}) can be summed to the same p-adic precision. |

| id | status | what the papers specify | what the code does | where | the fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LogShellFromBounds`<br>The log-shell I_v is given by an inner radius and a model log-volume | approximate | I_v = (p*_v)^{−1}·log(O×_{K_v}) ⊆ K_v, a specific compact Z_p-module, with μ_log(I_v) = log p* − (1/e + m/(ef)) log p; at an archimedean v, the closed disc of radius π. <br>*[IUTchIII] Def 1.1, Prop 1.2; [AbsTopIII] Def 5.4 (iii); [IUTchIV] Prop 1.2, 1.4 (ii)* | The radius printed is that of the largest p^λ·O_v the series argument puts inside I_v; μ_log uses the lower bounds for e and m. The archimedean log-volume is set to 0. | iut_lattice.c: iut_apply_log_link; iut_ops_iii.c: iut_log_shell_make; iut_core.c: iut_log_shell_volume | Follows from LocalFieldsOfK: with the true (e, f, m) the formula is exact. The archimedean term log π per factor is carried in the hull bound (Step (vii)) and should be shown on the shell as well. |
| `LogLinkMovesNoElements`<br>The log-link relabels copies; no element goes through a logarithm | open | log_v: O×_{†v} → †K_v, whose image becomes the additive module of the next copy ‡; the log-Kummer correspondence follows elements up the column and is only upper semi-compatible. <br>*[IUTchIII] Def 1.1 (iii), Prop 1.2 (iii), (iv), Prop 3.5* | The link copies Π_v and G_v, gives the units a new copy number and attaches the log-shells. Upper semi-compatibility is a table of three cases. | iut_lattice.c: iut_apply_log_link; iut_ops_iii.c: iut_log_link_strip, iut_upper_semi_compatibility | Open. With p-adic units to precision p^8 (already used for the Tate unit) the p-adic logarithm of a unit is a few lines; the first use would be to show log(q-unit) inside I_v at each v ∈ V^bad. |

| `InexplicitConstants`<br>η_prm, ξ_prm, H_unif, C_K, H_K are not given by the papers | asserted | [IUTchIV] only says that η_prm and ξ_prm ≥ 5 exist, and that H_unif, C_K, H_K exist for a compactly bounded subset; the exceptional set Exc_d is finite but not listed. <br>*[IUTchIV] Prop 1.6, Prop 2.1 (ii), Cor 2.2 (ii); [ExpEst] §1* | η_prm = 5·10^20 is borrowed from [ExpEst] (where it serves a sharper form of the prime number theorem); ξ_prm is used only through ξ_prm ≥ 5; Exc is tested by the two conditions the proof makes explicit; C_K is the constant of Thm 1.10 with e_mod = 1. | iut_ops.h: IUT_ETA_PRM_VALUE; iut_ops_iv.c: iut_cor22_compute | Open. | `ReductionToGeneralPosition`<br>From compactly bounded subsets to all curves: not modelled | open | Cor 2.3 obtains Vojta/abc for all hyperbolic curves from Cor 2.2 through [GenEll] (Belyi maps, compactly bounded subsets, bounded discrepancy classes). <br>*[IUTchIV] Cor 2.2 (i), Cor 2.3; [GenEll] Thm 2.1* | iut_cor23_bound evaluates the slack of one inequality; there is no notion of a compactly bounded subset or of ≈. | iut_ops_iv.c: iut_cor23_bound | Open.
